clue.text: Writer sees mother superior with a leg in the air

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
U stands for upper-class, i.e. socially superior

parts.words: with a leg in the air
parts.note: passant is the heraldic term for a beast walking with one foreleg raised

explanation.surface: A writer notices a Mother Superior oddly standing with one leg raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother superior' looks like a nun's title but splits in two. In heraldry a lion passant walks with one forepaw lifted, which the clue paints as 'a leg in the air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de Maupassant was a French author of short stories, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Mature wife in team

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for wife inside the word for team

parts.note: a team is a group of people working together

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a married woman playing on the side is the grown-up one.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to develop into an adult, the verbal phrase meaning exactly that.

clue.text: Small picture of something unimportant

explanation.surface: A tiny image of a trivial thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fig. is the short form of figure, an illustration in a book; and a fig is a trifle, as in not caring a fig.

clue.text: Dishonest about flying cat? OK

indicators.note: about means the word for dishonest goes around the other pieces

parts.note: fiddling means cheating or acting dishonestly, as in fiddling the books
air, as in air travel, means flying
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cheat dealing with an airborne cat is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying cat' pretends to be one odd creature; 'about' wraps the cheating word around both pieces, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair to middling means moderately good, neither bad nor great, the same as so-so.

clue.text: Work of genius? No

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is a masterpiece, the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work of genius' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'Work of' gives the wordplay and 'genius? No' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly, foolish person, the very opposite of a brilliant mind.

clue.text: Bag has flask in bottom

indicators.note: in puts the word for flask inside the word for bag

parts.note: to net is to bag or catch, as a fish
a Thermos is a vacuum flask, from the brand name

explanation.surface: A bag holds a flask down at the very bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the flask inside the bag, splitting it after its second letter; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, the one placed furthest down.

clue.text: Actor in 7 recalled self-criticism?

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the actor's name inside the answer to 7

parts.note: refers to the answer at 7 down, a musical work
Richard Gere is an American film actor

explanation.surface: An actor cast in a work is remembered for being hard on himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the actor inside the answer to 7, giving OGEREPUS, and 'recalled' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the conscience-like part of the mind judges and criticises one's own conduct, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Gives up on holding up work

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the held letters read upwards, i.e. backwards
holding means the letters are held inside the words Gives up on

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the effort of keeping a structure upright.
explanation.walkthrough: givES UP On holds SUPO, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, used especially of a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: A court procedure mostly seen in courts

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a trial is the procedure by which a court hears a case

explanation.surface: A legal process, mostly, takes place in courtrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' looks legal like the rest, but here it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central halls or courtyards in Roman houses and modern buildings.

clue.text: Open cut gets better

parts.note: overt means open, not concealed
rump is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: An open wound improves.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games to overtrump is to play a higher trump than an opponent, so to beat or surpass.

clue.text: Bishop enters "insane" plea, since that makes a difference

indicators.note: enters means the bishop's letter goes into the rearranged letters
insane signals that the following words are mixed up wildly

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop pleads insanity, since that may sway the verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insane' rearranges PLEA SINCE THAT, and 'enters' puts B in to make the full phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip the balance is to be the deciding factor, the thing that swings an outcome.

clue.text: Poet who prefers fancy square paper weight?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorative, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is short for square, as in Sloane Sq or the S of a grid square

explanation.surface: A poet who likes elaborate square-shaped stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper weight' reads as a desk object, but it means the clout of newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The influence newspapers wield over public opinion is the weight the papers carry.

clue.text: Have a beer, angel

parts.note: to sup is to drink, to have a drink
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: An invitation to an angel to enjoy a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: An angel in theatre is a financial backer of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer who funds a theatrical production is called an angel, i.e. a financial backer.

clue.text: Whisk in use after it makes a drink

indicators.note: to whisk is to stir rapidly, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A whisk is put to use after a drink is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whisk' looks like the kitchen tool, but it is the mixing signal for IN USE AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small perforated device holding loose leaves while they steep in hot water brews a cup.

clue.text: The watercourse doesn't start around fountain

parts.note: T' is the dialect form of the, as in northern England

indicators.note: around means the shortened watercourse is turned back to front
doesn't start means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a river is a natural watercourse

explanation.surface: The stream has dried up at its source near the fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' leaves IVER, which 'around' turns back. T' for 'the' is northern English dialect, as in 'on t' moor'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trevi in Rome is the most famous ornamental fountain in the world, an example of one.

clue.text: Hating or loving life, but not if given to moan

parts.note: to be into something is to love it, as in into jazz

indicators.note: but not means the following letters are taken out of life

parts.note: to rant is to moan noisily

explanation.surface: A grumbler either detests or loves life, provided they are not prone to complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life but not if' leaves LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwilling to accept others' views or ways is hostile to them, detesting them.

clue.text: France's place in continent usurped by middle east country

indicators.note: usurped by means one letter's place is taken over by others

parts.note: Africa is a continent
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: France's colonial position on a continent seized by a Middle Eastern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In AFRICA, the F's place is taken by ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is often simply called America, a nation.

clue.text: Capped teeth ultimately not original

indicators.note: capped means the top, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: pearlies, from pearly whites, is slang for teeth

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word not

explanation.surface: Teeth fitted with crowns are not, in the end, the ones you were born with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capped' suggests dental work; here it lops the P off PEARLIES to give EARLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The original version is the first, the one that came before all others.

clue.text: Oscar Peterson's first love in song about fan

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: first means the initial letter of Peterson's
in places the zero for love inside the turned word for song
about means the word for song is turned round

parts.note: a tune is a song or melody
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist's top love song is about an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: TUNE turned round is ENUT, with O inside to make ENOUT. Oscar Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist, so 'fan' reads as admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan out is to spread or unfold, as a hand of cards spreads.

clue.text: Sleepy river shown in drawing

indicators.note: shown in means the river's letter appears inside the other word

parts.note: teams drawing are tied, level on score
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A drowsy river appears in a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests a picture; here it means level in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy is weary and in need of rest.

clue.text: In Latin he translated a name for an apostle

indicators.note: In at the front means the following pieces go inside the rearranged letters
translated means the letters are turned into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: In Latin, he rendered a name for one of Christ's disciples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges LATIN HE into NATHIEL, and 'In' puts A and N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel, often identified with Bartholomew, was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.

clue.text: Ancient text from Munich in Germany

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words Munich in Germany

explanation.surface: An old manuscript comes from a Bavarian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The I Ching is the classic Chinese Book of Changes, an old divination text.

clue.text: During fast, unorthodox religious ceremony by the female priest?

indicators.note: by means the female pronoun is placed beside the rest
During means the religious pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
unorthodox means irregular, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or religious
a ritual is a religious ceremony
her is the pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: A woman priest conducts an irregular rite during a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges the fast into SFAT, and 'During' sets the religious pieces inside it; 'by' adds the female pronoun after.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessor or spiritual guide, often addressed as Father, is a priest, hence the question mark.

clue.text: It describes excessive intake of fizzy drink

indicators.note: describes, in the sense of drawing around, means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
OD is short for overdose, an excessive intake

explanation.surface: A clue claiming to explain taking in too much fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a crossword convention for sex appeal, SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated, a sparkling beverage.

clue.text: Love to come last in noisy game

indicators.note: to come last means the letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: loud means noisy
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A sweetheart finishes bottom in a rowdy pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game for children played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Varied nuts said to lead to hunger

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of said are jumbled

parts.note: greed is a hunger or craving for more

explanation.surface: Assorted nuts are said to make you hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food, but it signals a rearrangement of SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: To have varied, in the sense of differing in opinion, is to have been at odds.

clue.text: Clergyman soon appears after opening of church

indicators.note: after means the word for soon comes after the opening letter
opening of means the first letter of church

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A clergyman shows up soon after the church opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Are debtors men who regularly get backing?

indicators.note: backing means the chosen letters are read backwards
regularly means every other letter of men who is taken

explanation.surface: A question whether people in debt are men who keep getting support.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of MEN WHO are E, W, O, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in debt is to have money outstanding to another; the verb expresses that state.
